_note: THE NISSE CASE FILE. Edit freely. evidence[]: id, n (the number Agent Skeie says), title, desc (shown when found), kind (the pixel drawing), cat (Tracks|Objects|Testimony|Places|Signals|Threshold), region (only the hint for the unfound, never exact), src (where it comes from: trail:<find id>, trial:<id>, chest:<id>, book:<varde id>, page:<n>, quest:<id>, ncc:<agent>:<line index from 0>), unlockDay, weight (1..3, counts to Case solved %), th = [witch, cold, threshold] how much it supports each theory, at = [x,z] where its pin hangs. Theories: confidence = (prior(day) + sum of the found th) / total. Voice lines: run build/make_case.py after changing text.

theories.name: Stolen by the witch
theories.blurb: The cookies, the crumbs, the munching. She grew, and then they were gone.

theories.name: Hiding from the cold
theories.blurb: Warm fires, packed rucksacks, tiny doors. They simply went indoors.

theories.name: Called into the Threshold World
theories.blurb: Footprints that go in and never out. A hum from underneath. A warm light.

evidence.title: Tracks, six centimetres
evidence.desc: Six centimetres, left foot only. Three steps, then the snow simply stops having opinions. Nobody flew. Nobody dug.

evidence.title: One mitten, left-handed
evidence.desc: Knitted, red, thumb in a place no person has a thumb. Still warm. The right-hand one is, per Agent Skeie, a matter for the courts.

evidence.title: A lantern that lights itself
evidence.desc: Lit at noon, nobody home, the flame the colour of a held breath. It leans left. Everything else in the valley leans right.

evidence.title: The snowman nobody built
evidence.desc: Carrot nose, coal eyes, one red cap. Facing the church. It has not melted. It has not moved. As of this morning it also has a mitten.

evidence.title: The leaning cairn
evidence.desc: One stone is added every night. Nobody is adding them. The top stone is warm and points, politely, at the town.

evidence.title: Campfire, still warm
evidence.desc: Cold for three days, says the report. The embers disagree. Someone fed it. Someone small, with very good manners.

evidence.title: Rucksack, one thermos
evidence.desc: Packed for a long winter: thermos, spare cap, a note reading BACK BY SUPPER. Supper was nine days ago.

evidence.title: Door frame: 'STILL HERE'
evidence.desc: Scratched at the height of a very small person. Underneath, smaller still: 'NOT HERE.' Both look equally sincere.
evidence.region: the old cabins by the penstock

evidence.title: Message in a bottle
evidence.desc: 'GONE DOWN. WARM IN HERE. BRING PORRIDGE.' Handwriting: neat. Spelling: Norwegian. Water inside: none.
evidence.region: the far west, by the big stone

evidence.title: The humming rune stone
evidence.desc: Carved before the road, warm to the touch, counting under its breath. It has reached twenty-three. It always reaches twenty-three.
evidence.region: the far west, by the big stone

evidence.title: Tracks into the hillside
evidence.desc: Small boots, many pairs, in single file, walking straight into solid rock. They did not come out. The rock has been very polite about it.

evidence.title: Sled, pointing at the sea
evidence.desc: Rope frayed, seat dry, runners still wet from a slope that does not exist. Pointing at the fjord, and then, rather pointedly, below it.

evidence.title: Notebook: 'A cookie is a bill'
evidence.desc: Page 2, the church. Whoever wrote this knew about the cookies before we did. Signed M. Nobody will say which M.

evidence.title: Notebook: the practising trapdoor
evidence.desc: Page 4, the bridge. 'Something under it has been practising your voice.' Skeie asks that nobody answers it. Skeie asks that nobody practises back.

evidence.title: Notebook: the stone counts
evidence.desc: Page 6, Orresteinen. 'It was set down carefully, and then told to wait.' Told by whom? We have a form for that. It is not on the form.

evidence.title: Notebook: the leaning cairns
evidence.desc: Page 8. 'Each stone is somebody who stopped walking and decided to stay.' Please stop counting the stones. Please.

evidence.title: Notebook: the breathing wire
evidence.desc: Page 10. 'The hum is not electricity. Something is breathing through the wires.' Agent Moen has asked to be moved to a quieter desk. The desk is the same desk.

evidence.title: Notebook: the warm cellar door
evidence.desc: Page 11. 'A cellar door you have walked past a thousand times. It is warm to the touch. Do not knock.' We knocked. Do not.

evidence.title: Lanterns that count back
evidence.desc: Light the posts one, two, three, and a fourth lights itself from underneath. The statue smiles. We have not asked it to.

evidence.title: Bells that say takk
evidence.desc: Rung in order they play a carol. Rung wrong they say takk. Nobody has rung them wrong for an hour and they said it anyway.

evidence.title: The statue that aims
evidence.desc: Hit every target and its eyes open. Cold stone, warm eyes. They follow you all the way to the car park.

evidence.title: Stones in a ring
evidence.desc: Stand in the ring and your feet go warm and your shadow points the wrong way. Skeie measured it twice. Then he stopped measuring.

evidence.title: Footprints that glow
evidence.desc: Follow them and they lead down the great pipe to a hatch with no handle. The lack of a handle is, in this case, the point.

evidence.title: The valley that nobody entered
evidence.desc: A secret statue in a secret valley. All the footprints leading to it are small, and all of them are going in.

evidence.title: The statue by the egg-stone
evidence.desc: Every stone in the ring faces the boulder. The boulder faces down. This is the third thing in this valley that faces down.

evidence.title: The mirror at the quay
evidence.desc: Ring the bells across still water and the answer comes back from a second quay, on the other side of the mirror, in different weather.

evidence.title: A chest of porridge receipts
evidence.desc: Forty-one signed receipts for porridge delivered to 'the Under-Barn'. All paid in full. Nobody has ever heard of an Under-Barn.

evidence.title: Ledger of absent nisser
evidence.desc: A list of names, each ticked in red. Every tick is dated the first of December. The last line is blank, and waiting, and slightly warm.

evidence.title: Chest: 'DO NOT OPEN TWICE'
evidence.desc: We opened it once. It contained an apology. We are not opening it twice.

evidence.title: A chest of tiny boots
evidence.desc: Seventeen pairs. Left boots only. This matches a mitten we are currently keeping in the freezer.

evidence.title: A chest with a view
evidence.desc: Whoever hid it picked the best view in the valley, then installed the chest facing away from it. It faces the cellar.

evidence.title: Gingerbread, vintage
evidence.desc: A tin of ginger crumbs, Norwegian butter, and a note: 'Sorry, ate the rest. H.' It is a very large note.

evidence.title: Entry that stops mid-wo
evidence.desc: The last entry in the Hamrevarden book stops in the middle of a sentence. Where the sentence would continue, someone has drawn a very small door.

evidence.title: Entry in a tiny hand
evidence.desc: The size of a thumbnail, signed P. The tilt of the letters suggests the writer was standing on the pen.

evidence.title: Three signatures, one pen
evidence.desc: Three different hands, the ink still wet. The pen is on a string. The string is not tied to anything.

evidence.title: Weather report: 'WARM'
evidence.desc: Every other entry says brr. This one says WARM, underlined twice. It was minus eleven.

evidence.title: Signed by the whole valley
evidence.desc: A page of tiny signatures, all dated the first of December. Underneath: 'See you down there.' Underneath that: a smiley, drawn by something with very few fingers.

evidence.title: A wish list
evidence.desc: 'Please may we go home', in nine languages. The tenth line is in Nisse. We do not have a translator. We have Marit.

evidence.title: Marker nine: the mitten
evidence.desc: Evidence marker nine, one red mitten, recovered from the market. Left-handed. Warm. Eirik Vik wishes it noted that he did not touch it.

evidence.title: One red cap, size small
evidence.desc: Still warm. Pjusk-grade wool. Wearer: unknown. Owner: very much missed. Hanne Roll has labelled it THE CAP and will hear no more.

evidence.title: The lantern that turns
evidence.desc: The big nisse's lantern, photographed. Yesterday it pointed north. Today south-east. The pattern repeats every twenty-three hours.

evidence.title: Agent Roll's field notes
evidence.desc: 'Followed from the camp by a sound like a very small cough.' It followed her all the way to the gate. It is still in the car park.

evidence.title: Evidence bag: candle wax
evidence.desc: Church candle wax, still molten at minus eight. Fingerprints: none. Teeth marks: tiny. Haugen has asked if he may stop carrying it.

evidence.title: A thermos, never opened
evidence.desc: Gløgg, seventy-one degrees, sealed since the first of December. The date on the lid is tomorrow. Kari Lund says it is a nisse flask.

evidence.title: Director: 'It is a spiral'
evidence.desc: 'The pins form a pattern. It is not a good pattern. It is a spiral.' As of today the spiral leads to one point. The Director has asked us not to say which.

evidence.title: Skeie: 'The crumbs lead down'
evidence.desc: 'Down is the keyword.' Agent Skeie has since put a second coat on, indoors, and moved his chair nearer the door.

evidence.title: The hum says 'takk'
evidence.desc: Played backwards, it says thank you. Played forwards it says nothing, which is worse. Agent Moen has stopped playing it either way.

evidence.title: Lindtner: 'Big enough to hold something shut'
evidence.desc: 'You only need to be big to reach something high, or to hold something shut.' Nobody has asked what is being held shut. Everybody has thought about it.

evidence.title: Director: 'Called, not taken'
evidence.desc: 'The nisser were not taken. They were called.' The whole case turns on that sentence. The Director has had it framed, and turned to face the wall.

evidence.title: Lindtner: 'Follow the warm light'
evidence.desc: 'If you ever see a warm light there, follow it. It is them.' Filed under: instructions, unofficial. Next to the thermos, which is evidence.

Tracks: Interesting. Small tracks. Do not step in them. Do not step next to them either.
Tracks. Logged, measured, photographed. They are still going somewhere. I do not like where.
Another set of footprints that ends in nothing. I have started to take it personally.
Objects: Interesting. Do not touch it. I mean it. Into the bag. Not that bag.
An object, small, possibly warm. Please place it on the table, gently, as if it might apologise.
Into the bag it goes. If it moves in the night, that is not in my report.
Testimony: Testimony. Somebody wrote it down, which means somebody knew. I am underlining that.
A statement. Signed, dated, and slightly unsettling. Perfect for the board.
Words on paper. The most dangerous kind of evidence. They stay exactly where you put them. Until they do not.
Places: A place. Pinned. If the map starts to look like a clock face, nobody say anything.
Another location for the wall. I am running out of red string, and the wall is not running out of locations.
Noted, pinned, and marked do not visit alone. Which we will all ignore.
Signals: A signal. Faint, regular, and polite. I do not trust polite.
Strange signals logged. Moen says it is only the radio. Moen has not looked up from that radio since Tuesday.
That counts as a signal. It counts as several other things too, mostly to twenty-three.
Threshold: That one goes at the bottom of the board. Underneath everything else. Where it belongs.
This changes the direction of the string. Everyone, please, look down.
I will say it quietly, because the walls are listening. That is the evidence that matters.
batch: Several new items since your last visit. I have numbered them. Please do not rearrange them. Rearranged evidence goes strange.
You have been busy. The board is fuller. The string is shorter. I am not sure those two things should go together.
More evidence, all at once. I will need a bigger table, and possibly a smaller imagination.

25: Twenty-five percent. A quarter of a case. The other three quarters are, regrettably, the same size as the first.
A quarter of the board is filled. Please do not tell the Minister it was ever empty.
50: Fifty percent. We now know half of what happened, and it is the cosy half.
Halfway. The pins are making a shape. I will not say which shape. It is a spiral. I said it.
75: Seventy-five percent. I have started leaving the corridor lights on. For the building, you understand.
Three quarters. The string only runs one way now. Down.
hook: You have enough, now. Come and see me in the ops room. I have a job that is not in any manual.
The case is nearly closed, and what is left is not on any board. Come and see me. Bring a lantern.

thresh.text: That is the last one. I have laid every item on the board, and every string meets in the same place. Down.
Called, not taken. Not stolen, not hiding. I have been down there once. They are waiting, and they are warm. Somebody has to go and get them.
Case closed, in so far as it can be. The nisser are in the Threshold World. They answered a call. Now someone must answer theirs. Take the lantern, and follow the warm light.

witch.text: That is the last one, and I have a theory. The witch took them. Cookies, crumbs, a very large note.
Case closed. The witch did it. Please do not tell the witch. She is, as of the twelfth, no longer taking calls.

cold.text: That is the last one, and the board says they went indoors to keep warm.
Case closed. They hid from the cold. Very sensible. Nobody has ever hidden from the cold quite this thoroughly.

quest.title: The warm light
quest.ask: Officer, a word. The case is almost solved, and the part that is left is a door. Beneath Chris's flat there is a trapdoor, and beneath the trapdoor there is a cellar that was never on any plan. Go down. If you see a warm light, do not call out. Follow it.
quest.wait: The trapdoor under Chris's flat. A warm light, somewhere below it. Take your lantern, and do not answer if it says your name.
quest.done: You saw it. Then the case is solved. I will file it under weather, because nobody reads the weather. Thank you. The nisser, I think, would have said takk.
